claims.text: The intrinsic chemical complexity of Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu nanoparticles produces local compositional fluctuations.
Local compositional fluctuations cause a broadened, multi-step premelting and melting transition.
Chemically uniform single-metal nanoparticles exhibit sharp, singular melting behavior.
The initially solid Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu nanoparticles can be synthesized as a single solid-solution phase.
The proposed particle-size range is approximately 5–20 nm.
The constituent elements have differing individual melting characteristics.
Limited atomic mobility helps preserve compositionally fluctuating regions in the multielement nanoparticles.
Spatial compositional fluctuations create a distribution of local melting temperatures.
The distribution of local melting temperatures produces gradual, sequential melting rather than a uniform sharp transition.
Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu nanoparticles will show a broadened DSC melting range with multiple steps or inflection points.
In situ TEM will reveal phase-coexistence regions in the HEA nanoparticles during heating.
The proposed mechanism applies under rapid thermal annealing and pulsed heating or cooling.
Local-composition effects on melting are maximized for particles approximately 5–20 nm in size.
Bulk dimensions or extremely slow thermal ramps may allow mechanisms other than local compositional heterogeneity to dominate melting.
Transition breadth and the number of observable melting steps may depend on particle size, compositional inhomogeneity, and interatomic interactions.
A sharp, singular HEA transition with no significant broadening or multi-step features relative to the matched monometallic control would falsify the proposed broadening mechanism.
